observation_summary: The method ArrayUtils.addAll throws an ArrayStoreException when attempting to concatenate arrays of incompatible types, rather than validating the types and throwing a more appropriate exception like IllegalArgumentException.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is the absence of a validation check (guard) to ensure that the component types of the two input arrays are compatible before attempting to copy them into a new array. The current implementation blindly proceeds to System.arraycopy, which triggers an ArrayStoreException at runtime. Adding a check to validate the types and throw an IllegalArgumentException is a classic 'Checking' defect fix.
evidence_used: java.lang.ArrayStoreException: arraycopy: type mismatch: can not copy java.lang.Long[] into java.lang.Integer[]
It would be a lot clearer if the method threw an IlegalArgumentException or similar.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The core issue is not the logic of the array concatenation itself, but the lack of a guard to prevent an invalid operation.
While the method signature uses generics, the failure is due to internal type incompatibility during execution, not a mismatch in the contract between caller and callee.
